title: Can a quantum algorithm solve exact Euclidean SVP in polynomial time?
formal: Is there a bounded-error quantum algorithm that, from a binary-encoded integer basis of a lattice, finds a nonzero vector of minimum Euclidean length in time polynomial in the input length?
context:
The Wikipedia item also asks about classical algorithms. Exact classical SVP is NP-hard under randomized reductions; polynomial-factor approximation and single-exponential algorithms with polynomial space are different targets.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: A central test of quantum algorithms against worst-case lattice hardness.
